claim: TRRAP belongs to the phosphoinositide 3 kinase-related kinases (PIKK) family
source: Structurally, TRRAP belongs to the phosphoinositide 3 kinase-related kinases (PIKK) family but is the only member classified as a pseudokinase.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a structural classification of TRRAP.

claim: TRRAP is the only PIKK family member classified as a pseudokinase
source: Structurally, TRRAP belongs to the phosphoinositide 3 kinase-related kinases (PIKK) family but is the only member classified as a pseudokinase.
evidence: This is explicitly stated in the abstract and introduction.

claim: The triple T (TTT) complex is essential for PIKK stabilization and activity
source: Recent studies established that a dedicated HSP90 co-chaperone, the triple T (TTT) complex, is essential for PIKK stabilization and activity.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: TELO2 promotes TRRAP assembly into SAGA and TIP60 in human colorectal cancer cells
source: Here, using endogenous auxin-inducible degron alleles, we show that the TTT subunit TELO2 promotes TRRAP assembly into SAGA and TIP60 in human colorectal cancer cells (CRCs).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 1G and H.

claim: TELO2 contributes to TRRAP regulatory roles in CRC cells, most notably of MYC target genes
source: Transcriptomic analysis revealed that TELO2 contributes to TRRAP regulatory roles in CRC cells, most notably of MYC target genes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: TELO2 and TRRAP depletion induces the expression of type I interferon genes
source: Surprisingly, TELO2 and TRRAP depletion also induced the expression of type I interferon genes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by RNA-seq and RT-qPCR data in Figure 2.

claim: TRRAP directly represses the transcription of IRF9
source: Using a combination of nascent RNA, antibody-targeted chromatin profiling (CUT&RUN), ChIP, and kinetic analyses, we propose a model by which TRRAP directly represses the transcription of IRF9, which encodes a master regulator of interferon-stimulated genes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by multiple experimental approaches including CUT&RUN (Figure 5E), nascent RNA (Figure 6A), and ChIP (Figure 6B).

claim: IRF9 encodes a master regulator of interferon-stimulated genes
source: Using a combination of nascent RNA, antibody-targeted chromatin profiling (CUT&RUN), ChIP, and kinetic analyses, we propose a model by which TRRAP directly represses the transcription of IRF9, which encodes a master regulator of interferon-stimulated genes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and is consistent with established knowledge about IRF9's role in the ISGF3 complex.

claim: TRRAP has an unexpected transcriptional repressor role
source: We have therefore uncovered an unexpected transcriptional repressor role for TRRAP, which we propose contributes to its tumorigenic activity.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a conclusion from the experimental findings.

claim: TRRAP's repressor role contributes to its tumorigenic activity
source: We have therefore uncovered an unexpected transcriptional repressor role for TRRAP, which we propose contributes to its tumorigenic activity.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the findings about ISG repression in cancer cells.

claim: SAGA carries histone acetyltransferase (HAT) and de-ubiquitination (DUB) activities
source: SAGA carries histone acetyltransferase (HAT) and de-ubiquitination (DUB) activities, which preferentially target histone H3 and H2B, respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge about SAGA complex.

claim: SAGA delivers TBP to specific promoters, stimulating pre-initiation complex (PIC) assembly
source: Similar to the general transcription factor TFIID, with which it shares four core TAF subunits in humans, SAGA delivers TBP to specific promoters, stimulating pre-initiation complex (PIC) assembly.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge about SAGA function.

claim: TIP60 carries HAT activity
source: TIP60 also carries HAT activity and, through the EP400 subunit, catalyzes deposition of the H2A.Z variant.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge about TIP60 complex.

claim: TIP60 acetylates histones H4 and H2A, as well as the histone variant H2A.Z
source: TIP60 acetylates histones H4 and H2A, as well as the histone variant H2A.Z.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge about TIP60 activity.

claim: SAGA and TIP60 share one component, named TRRAP in mammals or Tra1 in yeast
source: SAGA and TIP60 share one component, named TRRAP in mammals or Tra1 in yeast (Grant et al., 1998; Vassilev et al., 1998; Allard et al., 1999; Saleh et al., 1998).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The primary role of Tra1/TRRAP is to recruit SAGA and TIP60 to specific promoters upon binding of an activator
source: The primary role of Tra1/TRRAP is to recruit SAGA and TIP60 to specific promoters upon binding of an activator.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge about TRRAP function.

claim: TRRAP was initially discovered as a coactivator for the c-MYC and E2F transcription factors
source: TRRAP was initially discovered as a coactivator for the c-MYC and E2F transcription factors and is essential for their oncogenic activities (McMahon et al., 1998).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: TRRAP is essential for the oncogenic activities of c-MYC and E2F
source: TRRAP was initially discovered as a coactivator for the c-MYC and E2F transcription factors and is essential for their oncogenic activities (McMahon et al., 1998).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Many additional activators require Tra1 or TRRAP to stimulate transcription initiation
source: Further work demonstrated that many additional activators require Tra1 or TRRAP to stimulate transcription initiation (Park et al., 2001; Bouchard et al., 2001; Lang et al., 2001; Deleu et al., 2001; Ard et al., 2002; Lang and Hearing, 2003; Memedula and Belmont, 2003; Knutson and Hahn, 2011; Lin et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with multiple supporting citations.

claim: Tra1 physically interacts with the transactivation domain of activators in vivo in yeast
source: Work in yeast demonstrated that Tra1 physically interacts with the transactivation domain of activators in vivo (Brown et al., 2001; Bhaumik and Green, 2001; Bhaumik et al., 2004; Fishburn et al., 2005; Reeves and Hahn, 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: TRRAP is essential for cell proliferation
source: However, the direct regulatory roles of Tra1/TRRAP have been challenging to study because TRRAP is essential for cell proliferation and early embryonic development in mice (Herceg et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: TRRAP is essential for early embryonic development in mice
source: However, the direct regulatory roles of Tra1/TRRAP have been challenging to study because TRRAP is essential for cell proliferation and early embryonic development in mice (Herceg et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: TRRAP lacks all catalytic residues
source: However, TRRAP lacks all catalytic residues and is therefore the sole pseudokinase of this family (reviewed in Elías-Villalobos et al., 2019a).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: PIKKs require a dedicated HSP90 co-chaperone, the triple T (TTT) complex, for their stabilization and incorporation into active complexes
source: Elegant studies have demonstrated that PIKKs require a dedicated HSP90 co-chaperone, the triple T (TTT) complex, for their stabilization and incorporation into active complexes (Takai et al., 2007; Anderson et al., 2008; Takai et al., 2010; Hurov et al., 2010; Kaizuka et al., 2010; Izumi et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with multiple supporting citations.

claim: TTT is composed of three conserved, specific subunits, TELO2, TTI1, and TTI2
source: TTT was initially discovered in the fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe and is composed of three conserved, specific subunits, TELO2, TTI1, and TTI2 (Takai et al., 2010; Hayashi et al., 2007; Shevchenko et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: TTT recruits HSP90 through the phosphorylation-dependent interaction of TELO2 with the R2TP complex
source: Mechanistically, TTT recruits HSP90 through the phosphorylation-dependent interaction of TELO2 with the R2TP complex, formed by RPAP3, PIH1D1, and the AAA+ ATPases RUVBL1 and RUVBL2 (Horejsí et al., 2010; Hořejší et al., 2014; Pal et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Auxin addition induces a rapid and robust depletion of TELO2AID, whose levels become undetectable after 4 hr of treatment
source: We found that auxin addition induces a rapid and robust depletion of either TELO2AID or AIDTRRAP, whose levels become undetectable after 4 hr of treatment (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by Western blot data in Figure 1A and B.

claim: Auxin addition induces a rapid and robust depletion of AIDTRRAP, whose levels become undetectable after 4 hr of treatment
source: We found that auxin addition induces a rapid and robust depletion of either TELO2AID or AIDTRRAP, whose levels become undetectable after 4 hr of treatment (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by Western blot data in Figure 1A and B.

claim: Depletion of either TELO2 or TRRAP progressively decreases the proliferation rate of HCT116 cells
source: Depletion of either TELO2 or TRRAP progressively decreases the proliferation rate of HCT116 cells (Figure 1C and D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C and D), consistent with previous results in mice (Herceg et al., 2001; Takai et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by proliferation assay data in Figure 1C and D.

claim: Prolonged TELO2 depletion reduces the steady-state levels of the TRRAP, ATM, ATR, and mTOR proteins
source: As expected, prolonged TELO2 depletion reduces the steady-state levels of the TRRAP, ATM, ATR, and mTOR proteins and impairs mTORC1 activity, as illustrated with p70-S6K phosphorylation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by Western blot data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Prolonged TELO2 depletion impairs mTORC1 activity
source: As expected, prolonged TELO2 depletion reduces the steady-state levels of the TRRAP, ATM, ATR, and mTOR proteins and impairs mTORC1 activity, as illustrated with p70-S6K phosphorylation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by Western blot data showing reduced p70-S6K phosphorylation in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Prolonged TRRAP depletion reduces the expression of the Cyclin A2 (CCNA2) gene
source: Similarly, prolonged TRRAP depletion reduces the expression of the Cyclin A2 (CCNA2) gene (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F), which is a known target of TRRAP (Wurdak et al., 2010; Tapias et al., 2014; Herceg et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Endogenous TELO2 is detected in cytoplasmic extracts, but not in nuclear extracts
source: Cellular fractionation followed by Western blot analysis showed that endogenous TELO2 is detected in cytoplasmic extracts (CE), but not in nuclear extracts (NE) (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by Western blot data in Figure 1E.

claim: TRRAP is predominantly nuclear
source: In contrast, TRRAP is predominantly nuclear (Figure 1E), consistent with its function and published immunofluorescence microscopy staining (Wurdak et al., 2010; Wang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by Western blot data in Figure 1E and citations.

claim: TELO2 interacts specifically with the cytoplasmic fraction of TRRAP, but not the nuclear fraction
source: Immunoprecipitation of TRRAP from each compartment showed that TELO2 interacts specifically with the cytoplasmic fraction of TRRAP, but not the nuclear fraction (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunoprecipitation data in Figure 1F.

claim: TELO2 depletion primarily affects nuclear TRRAP levels
source: We noticed that TELO2 depletion primarily affects nuclear TRRAP levels (Figure 1E and F), suggesting that TELO2 binds newly synthesized TRRAP in the cytoplasm to promote its assembly into SAGA and TIP60, which would then be imported into the nucleus.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by Western blot and immunoprecipitation data in Figure 1E and F.

claim: TELO2 depletion reduces the interaction between TRRAP and SUPT3H
source: Immunoprecipitation of the SAGA-specific subunit SUPT3H showed a reduced interaction with TRRAP upon TELO2 depletion (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunoprecipitation data in Figure 1G.

claim: TELO2 depletion does not affect the interaction between SUPT3H and the SAGA subunits SUPT7L, TADA1, TADA3, SGF29, and TAF10
source: In contrast, TELO2 depletion did not affect the interaction between SUPT3H and the SAGA subunits SUPT7L, TADA1, TADA3, SGF29, and TAF10 (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunoprecipitation data in Figure 1G.

claim: TELO2 depletion reduces the interaction between TRRAP and EP400
source: Similarly, we observed a reduced interaction between TRRAP and the TIP60-specific component EP400 upon TELO2 depletion (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunoprecipitation data in Figure 1H.

claim: Reducing the levels of TRRAP within SAGA does not affect the interaction between SUPT3H and all the other SAGA subunits tested
source: Interestingly, this analysis also revealed that reducing the levels of TRRAP within SAGA does not affect the interaction between SUPT3H, the bait, and all the other SAGA subunits tested (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunoprecipitation data in Figure 1G.

claim: TRRAP might be dispensable for SAGA's overall integrity and function
source: This observation suggests that TRRAP, despite being about 420 kDa and the largest subunit of SAGA, might be dispensable for SAGA's overall integrity and function, as demonstrated in yeast (Elías-Villalobos et al., 2019b; Helmlinger et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the results as an inference from the immunoprecipitation data and supported by citations.

claim: CHOP and HERPUD are strongly induced upon treating HCT116 cells with thapsigargin
source: As expected, we found that two such genes, CHOP and HERPUD, are strongly induced upon treating HCT116 cells with thapsigargin (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by RT-qPCR data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: CHOP and HERPUD induction decreases about twofold upon RNAi-mediated knockdown of the SAGA core subunit SUPT20H
source: Consistent with previous work, their induction decreases about twofold upon RNAi-mediated knockdown of the SAGA core subunit SUPT20H compared with control siRNA transfections.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by RT-qPCR data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: CHOP and HERPUD are robustly induced in AIDTRRAP cells, irrespective of auxin treatment
source: In contrast, despite robust TRRAP depletion (Figure 1B), we observed a robust induction of both CHOP and HERPUD in AIDTRRAP cells, irrespective of auxin treatment (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by RT-qPCR data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: TRRAP does not have a major contribution to SAGA integrity and function at CHOP and HERPUD genes
source: Taken together, these results suggest that TRRAP does not have a major contribution to SAGA integrity and function at these genes.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an inference from the RT-qPCR data.

claim: TRRAP is not a core subunit of SAGA in human cells
source: Thus, despite its large size and absence of catalytic activity, TRRAP is presumably not a core subunit of SAGA in human cells, consistent with recent structural studies revealing its peripheral localization within the complex (Papai et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2020; Herbst et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the results as an inference from the functional data and supported by citations to structural studies.

claim: Using a 1% false discovery rate (FDR) cutoff, 2227 transcripts change levels upon TRRAP depletion
source: Using a 1% false discovery rate (FDR) cutoff, we identified 2227 transcripts whose levels change upon TRRAP depletion, whereas only 470 transcripts depend on TELO2 (Supplementary files 1 and 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by RNA-seq data.

claim: Using a 1% false discovery rate (FDR) cutoff, 470 transcripts depend on TELO2
source: Using a 1% false discovery rate (FDR) cutoff, we identified 2227 transcripts whose levels change upon TRRAP depletion, whereas only 470 transcripts depend on TELO2 (Supplementary files 1 and 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by RNA-seq data.

claim: There is a positive correlation between the gene expression changes caused by TELO2 and TRRAP depletion (Pearson's correlation coefficient r = 0.66)
source: Comparing these two datasets, we found a positive correlation between the gene expression changes caused by TELO2 and TRRAP depletion (Pearson's correlation coefficient r = 0.66) (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by the scatter plot in Figure 2A.

claim: A majority of genes whose expression decreases upon TELO2 depletion (152/212) are downregulated in TRRAP-depleted cells
source: Indeed, a majority of genes whose expression decreases upon TELO2 depletion (152/212) are downregulated in TRRAP-depleted cells (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by the Venn diagram in Figure 2B.

claim: Almost half of the genes whose expression increases upon TELO2 depletion (118/258) are upregulated in TRRAP-depleted cells
source: Likewise, almost half of the genes whose expression increases upon TELO2 depletion (118/258) are upregulated in TRRAP-depleted cells (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by the Venn diagram in Figure 2B.

claim: TELO2 and TRRAP promote the expression of the CCNA2 and MYB genes
source: We observed that TELO2 and TRRAP promote the expression of the CCNA2 and MYB genes, which encode the cell cycle regulator Cyclin A2 and the Myb transcription factor, respectively (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E and F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by RT-qPCR data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E and F.

claim: TELO2 and TRRAP activate GNL3 and MIR17HG, which are well-characterized MYC target genes
source: TELO2 and TRRAP also activate two well-characterized MYC targets genes, GNL3 and the MiR-17-92a-1 Cluster Host Gene MIR17HG (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E and F; Jaenicke et al., 2016; Li et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by RT-qPCR data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E and F and citations.

claim: Both TELO2 and TRRAP inhibit the expression of KRT20
source: Conversely, both TELO2 and TRRAP inhibit the expression of KRT20, a marker of differentiated epithelial cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G and H).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by RT-qPCR data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1G and H.

claim: The set of genes downregulated upon TRRAP depletion is mostly enriched for MYC or E2Fs target genes
source: We found that the set of genes downregulated upon TRRAP depletion is mostly enriched for MYC or E2Fs target genes (Figure 2C, lower panels).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by GSEA analysis in Figure 2C.

claim: TRRAP is a coactivator of the c-MYC and E2Fs transcription factors in HCT116 cells
source: This observation confirms that TRRAP is a coactivator of the c-MYC and E2Fs transcription factors in HCT116 cells, similar to its role in other mammalian cell types.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a conclusion from the GSEA analysis.

claim: The set of genes activated by TELO2 is enriched for MYC or E2Fs targets
source: Remarkably, the set of genes activated by TELO2 was also enriched for MYC or E2Fs targets, with comparable enrichment scores (Figure 2C, upper panels).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by GSEA analysis in Figure 2C.

claim: TELO2 is a novel regulator of the c-MYC and E2Fs transcriptional factors in HCT116 CRC cells
source: Therefore, TELO2 is a novel regulator of the c-MYC and E2Fs transcriptional factors in HCT116 CRC cells, presumably through its role in promoting TRRAP incorporation into the SAGA and TIP60 coactivator complexes.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a conclusion from the GSEA analysis.

claim: Differentially expressed genes are quantitatively more affected upon TRRAP depletion than upon TELO2 depletion
source: First, differentially expressed genes are quantitatively more affected upon TRRAP depletion than upon TELO2 depletion (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by RNA-seq data visualized in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C and D.

claim: TRRAP regulates a higher number of genes than TELO2
source: Second, TRRAP regulates a higher number of genes than TELO2 (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by RNA-seq data visualized in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C and D.

claim: Nearly one-third of the 97 ISGs (28/97) from the IFNα response hallmark is differentially expressed in the absence of TELO2 and TRRAP
source: Using an adjusted p-value threshold of 0.05, we found that nearly one-third of the 97 ISGs (28/97) from the IFNα response hallmark is differentially expressed in the absence of TELO2 and TRRAP (Figure 2C, right panels).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by GSEA analysis in Figure 2C.

claim: Most ISGs (23/28) are repressed by TELO2 and TRRAP
source: However, in contrast to the activation of MYC and E2Fs targets, we observed that most ISGs (23/28) are repressed by TELO2 and TRRAP (23/28), whereas they activate the expression of only a few ISGs (5/28) (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by the heatmap in Figure 2D.

claim: The ISG response is the most highly enriched category in the set of genes repressed by TELO2 (normalized enrichment score [NES] = 2.51)
source: Accordingly, the ISG response is the most highly enriched category in the set of genes repressed by TELO2 (normalized enrichment score [NES] = 2.51) and TRRAP (NES = 2.28) (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by GSEA analysis in Figure 2C.

claim: The ISG response is the most highly enriched category in the set of genes repressed by TRRAP (NES = 2.28)
source: Accordingly, the ISG response is the most highly enriched category in the set of genes repressed by TELO2 (normalized enrichment score [NES] = 2.51) and TRRAP (NES = 2.28) (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by GSEA analysis in Figure 2C.

claim: IRF7, OAS1, and IFIT1 exhibit increased mRNA levels upon depletion of either TELO2 or TRRAP
source: All three genes exhibit increased mRNA levels upon depletion of either TELO2 or TRRAP (Figure 2E and F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by RT-qPCR data in Figure 2E and F.

claim: TRRAP depletion causes a stronger induction of ISGs compared to TELO2
source: Compared to TELO2, we observed that TRRAP depletion causes a stronger induction of ISGs (Figure 2D–F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 2D–F.

claim: None of the TELO2- or TRRAP-regulated ISGs have AHR-binding motifs within 10 kb of the transcription start sites, except IFIT3
source: However, we found that none of the TELO2- or TRRAP-regulated ISGs have AHR-binding motifs within 10 kb of the transcription start sites (TSS), except IFIT3.
evidence: This is stated in the results based on analysis of cis-regulatory features.

claim: Auxin treatment of parental HCT116 cells, expressing TIR1 only, does not affect IRF7, OAS1, and IFIT1 expression
source: Finally, we verified that auxin treatment of parental HCT116 cells, expressing TIR1 only, does not affect IRF7, OAS1, and IFIT1 expression (Figure 2E and F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by RT-qPCR data in Figure 2E and F.

claim: ISGs are specifically induced in response to TELO2 and TRRAP depletion
source: Altogether, these results show that ISGs are specifically induced in response to TELO2 and TRRAP depletion, indicating that TELO2 and TRRAP repress ISG expression in unstimulated HCT116 CRC cancer cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a conclusion from the RT-qPCR and RNA-seq data.

claim: TELO2 and TRRAP repress ISG expression in unstimulated HCT116 CRC cancer cells
source: Altogether, these results show that ISGs are specifically induced in response to TELO2 and TRRAP depletion, indicating that TELO2 and TRRAP repress ISG expression in unstimulated HCT116 CRC cancer cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a conclusion from the RT-qPCR and RNA-seq data.

claim: Neither the PRR nor the IFN-I signaling pathways are activated upon TRRAP depletion
source: We found that neither the PRR nor the IFN-I signaling pathways are activated upon TRRAP depletion.
evidence: This is stated in the results based on Western blot analysis of phosphorylation status.

claim: There is no detectable increase in IRF3 Ser396 phosphorylation upon TRRAP depletion
source: Western blot analyses showed no detectable increase in IRF3 Ser396 phosphorylation and STAT1 Ser727 phosphorylation upon TRRAP depletion (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by Western blot data in Figure 3B.

claim: There is no detectable increase in STAT1 Ser727 phosphorylation upon TRRAP depletion
source: Western blot analyses showed no detectable increase in IRF3 Ser396 phosphorylation and STAT1 Ser727 phosphorylation upon TRRAP depletion (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by Western blot data in Figure 3B.

claim: Poly(I:C) induces IRF3 and STAT1 phosphorylation in AIDTRRAP HCT116 cell lines
source: As a control, we treated AIDTRRAP cells with a double-stranded (ds) RNA mimic, polyinosinic acid:polycytidylic acid (poly(I:C)), which is a potent IFN-I inducer (Field et al., 1967). As expected, poly(I:C) induced IRF3 and STAT1 phosphorylation, validating our experimental conditions and indicating that a functional innate immune response can be triggered in AIDTRRAP HCT116 cell lines.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by Western blot data in Figure 3B and a citation.

claim: TRRAP depletion induces ISG expression without activating the PRR and IFN-I signaling pathways
source: Therefore, TRRAP depletion induces ISG expression without activating the PRR and IFN-I signaling pathways and presumably acts downstream of the IRF3 and IRF7 transcription regulators.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a conclusion from the Western blot data.

claim: The IRF7 and IRF9 transcription factors accumulate earlier than the dsRNA sensor DDX58 (RIG-I) in TRRAP-depleted cells
source: While performing this analysis, we noticed that different innate immune response factors accumulate with apparently distinct kinetics in TRRAP-depleted cells (Figure 3C and D). Specifically, the IRF7 and IRF9 transcription factors accumulate earlier than the dsRNA sensor DDX58 (RIG-I).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by Western blot data in Figure 3C and D.

claim: The relative mRNA levels of IRF9 increase about twofold already 5 hr after auxin addition
source: This analysis showed that the relative mRNA levels of IRF9 change rapidly, increasing about twofold already 5 hr after auxin addition (Figure 3E), which is concomitant with the loss of a detectable TRRAP signal by Western blot (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by RT-qPCR data in Figure 3E.

claim: IRF9 levels do not increase noticeably beyond 10 hr of TRRAP depletion and reach a plateau around fourfold
source: However, IRF9 levels do not increase noticeably beyond 10 hr of TRRAP depletion and reach a plateau around fourfold.
evidence: This is stated in the results based on RT-qPCR data.

claim: IRF7 mRNA levels gradually increase over a period of 24 hr of TRRAP depletion
source: In contrast, IRF7 mRNA levels gradually increase over a period of 24 hr of TRRAP depletion and accumulate with a slight delay compared to IRF9 (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by RT-qPCR data in Figure 3E.

claim: The expression of ISGF3 targets, including RIG-I, OAS1, IFIT1, and MX1, gradually increases upon TRRAP depletion
source: Finally, we found that the expression of ISGF3 targets, including RIG-I, OAS1, IFIT1, and MX1, gradually increases upon TRRAP depletion, similar to IRF7 (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by RT-qPCR data in Figure 3E.

claim: The IRF9 transcription factor is induced earlier than its target genes, including IRF7
source: Altogether, the progressive accumulation of ISGs indicates that this phenotype appears early after the loss of TRRAP, rather than at late time points. Furthermore, this kinetic analysis indicates that the IRF9 transcription factor is induced earlier than its target genes, including IRF7.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a conclusion from the kinetic RT-qPCR analysis.

claim: IRF9 levels increase about fourfold upon TRRAP depletion
source: Here, our RNA-seq, quantitative RT-PCR, and Western blot analyses indicate that IRF9 levels increase about fourfold (Supplementary file 2, Figure 3C and E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by multiple types of data.

claim: STAT1 and STAT2 levels do not change upon TRRAP depletion
source: In contrast, STAT1 and STAT2 levels do not change (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by Western blot data in Figure 3B and C.

claim: TRRAP depletion induces a progressive accumulation of IRF9, but neither activation nor overexpression of its partners STAT1 and STAT2
source: Thus, TRRAP depletion induces a progressive accumulation of IRF9, but neither activation nor overexpression of its partners STAT1 and STAT2.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a conclusion from the Western blot and RT-qPCR data.

claim: U-ISGF3 induces the transcription of a subset of 29 ISGs
source: Work in both normal and cancer cells demonstrated that IRF9 can assemble with unphosphorylated STAT1 and STAT2 to form the unphosphorylated ISGF3 (U-ISGF3) complex. U-ISGF3 induces the transcription of a subset of 29 ISGs and sustains their prolonged, constitutive expression (Cheon et al., 2013; Sung et al., 2015; Platanitis et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the results with supporting citations.

claim: The phosphorylated form of ISGF3 activates an additional 49 ISGs upon acute IFN-I signaling
source: In contrast, the phosphorylated form of ISGF3 activates an additional 49 ISGs upon acute IFN-I signaling (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the results with a reference to Figure 4A.

claim: TRRAP regulates the mRNA levels of about a third of all ISGs (39/113), mostly negatively (30/39)
source: Using an adjusted p-value threshold of 0.05, we found that TRRAP regulates the mRNA levels of about a third of all ISGs (39/113), mostly negatively (30/39) (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by RNA-seq data in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: TRRAP primarily represses U-ISGF3-dependent genes, while ISGF3-dependent genes remain largely unaffected
source: To compare the effect of TRRAP on U-ISGF3- and ISGF3-regulated genes, we plotted each set separately and observed that TRRAP primarily represses U-ISGF3-dependent genes, while ISGF3-dependent genes remain largely unaffected (compare green and orange violin plots, Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by the violin plots in Figure 4B.

claim: The expression of 20 of the 28 U-ISGF3-dependent genes increases at least 1.5-fold in TRRAP-depleted cells
source: Specifically, the expression of 20 of the 28 U-ISGF3-dependent genes increases at least 1.5-fold in TRRAP-depleted cells, whereas only 6 of the 35 ISGF3-dependent genes are induced.
evidence: This is stated in the results based on RNA-seq data analysis.

claim: The interferon-stimulated response element (ISRE) is the most enriched motif in the promoter regions of TRRAP-regulated ISGs
source: This analysis identified the interferon-stimulated response element (ISRE) as the most enriched motif in the promoter regions of TRRAP-regulated ISGs (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by motif analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: ISREs are specifically recognized by IRF9 homo- or heterodimers, as well as the ISGF3 complex
source: ISREs are specifically recognized by IRF9 homo- or heterodimers, as well as the ISGF3 complex (Negishi et al., 2018), suggesting that IRF9 upregulation is sufficient to induce ISG expression in TRRAP-depleted cells, independently of IFN-I signaling.
evidence: This is stated in the results with a supporting citation.

claim: IRF7-binding sites are the second most enriched motifs in the set of TRRAP-regulated ISGs
source: IRF7-binding sites were the second most enriched motifs in the set of TRRAP-regulated ISGs.
evidence: This is stated in the results based on motif analysis.

claim: IRF7 protein levels progressively accumulate upon TRRAP depletion
source: In agreement with this observation, IRF7 protein levels progressively accumulate upon TRRAP depletion (Figure 3D), consistent with the 2.6-fold increase observed by RNA-seq (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by Western blot data in Figure 3D and RNA-seq data.

claim: TRRAP binds 12 of the 28 annotated U-ISGs
source: Analyzing the overlap between TRRAP binding and regulatory effect revealed that TRRAP binds 12 of the 28 annotated U-ISGs (Figure 5F and Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by CUT&RUN-seq data in Figure 5F.

claim: TRRAP binds and represses eight U-ISGs whose expression increases at least 1.5-fold upon TRRAP depletion
source: These include eight genes whose expression increases at least 1.5-fold upon TRRAP depletion, suggesting a direct inhibitory effect (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by CUT&RUN-seq and RNA-seq data in Figure 5F.

claim: TRRAP binds and represses DDX58 (RIG-I), IRF7, and IRF9
source: Notably, TRRAP binds and represses several genes with pivotal roles in innate immune responses, such as the dsRNA sensor DDX58, also known as RIG-I, as well as the IRF7 and IRF9 transcription factors (Figure 5E and F), which mediate the transcriptional induction of downstream effectors of type I IFN signaling.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by CUT&RUN-seq data in Figure 5E and F.

claim: TRRAP directly binds to the promoter regions of IRF7 and IRF9 in HCT116 cells
source: In conclusion, an innovative chromatin profiling technique allowed us to demonstrate that TRRAP directly binds to the promoter regions of some, but not all U-ISGs in HCT116 cells, most importantly IRF7 and IRF9, which encode master regulators of their expression.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a conclusion from the CUT&RUN-seq data.

claim: The levels of newly synthesized IRF7 pre-mRNAs increase about 1.8-fold in the absence of TRRAP
source: We found that the levels of newly synthesized IRF7 and IRF9 pre-mRNAs increase about 1.8- and 1.6-fold in the absence of TRRAP, respectively (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by nascent RNA data in Figure 6A.

claim: The levels of newly synthesized IRF9 pre-mRNAs increase about 1.6-fold in the absence of TRRAP
source: We found that the levels of newly synthesized IRF7 and IRF9 pre-mRNAs increase about 1.8- and 1.6-fold in the absence of TRRAP, respectively (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by nascent RNA data in Figure 6A.

claim: TRRAP inhibits IRF7 and IRF9 mRNA synthesis
source: We conclude that TRRAP inhibits IRF7 and IRF9 mRNA synthesis, suggesting that TRRAP is a transcriptional repressor of these genes.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a conclusion from the nascent RNA data.

claim: RNA polymerase II recruitment increases at IRF7 and IRF9 at all time points after auxin addition compared to control conditions
source: ChIP-qPCR revealed that RNA polymerase II recruitment increases at IRF7 and IRF9 at all time points after auxin addition compared to control conditions (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by ChIP-qPCR data in Figure 6B.

claim: Auxin induces a loss of TRRAP binding to IRF7 and IRF9 promoters
source: CUT&RUN-qPCR experiments confirmed the robust and specific binding of TRRAP to the promoter regions of both IRF7 and IRF9 compared to control IgGs and showed that auxin induces a loss of its binding (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by CUT&RUN-qPCR data in Figure 6C.

claim: RNA polymerase II occupancy increases already 7 hr after auxin addition, while TRRAP is already undetectable at IRF7 and IRF9 promoters
source: Notably, RNA polymerase II occupancy increases already 7 hr after auxin addition, while TRRAP is already undetectable at their promoters, suggesting that TRRAP depletion rapidly induces the transcription of both genes.
evidence: This is stated in the results based on ChIP-qPCR and CUT&RUN-qPCR data.

claim: TRRAP binds to the IRF7 and IRF9 promoters and represses their transcription
source: Altogether, CUT&RUN profiling, nascent RNA, and kinetic analysis of RNA polymerase II occupancy indicate that TRRAP binds to the IRF7 and IRF9 promoters and represses their transcription.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a conclusion from multiple experimental approaches.

claim: TRRAP is a direct transcriptional repressor of master regulators of ISG expression in HCT116 cells
source: We thus conclude that, unexpectedly, TRRAP is a direct transcriptional repressor of master regulators of ISG expression in HCT116 cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a conclusion from the combined data.

claim: Following initial depletion, TRRAP progressively reaccumulates within a few hours after washing out auxin from the media
source: Western blot analyses confirmed that, following initial depletion, TRRAP progressively reaccumulates within a few hours after washing out auxin from the media (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by Western blot data in Figure 7B.

claim: TRRAP binding to IRF7 and IRF9 progressively reappears upon auxin removal
source: CUT&RUN followed by qPCR showed that TRRAP binding to IRF7 and IRF9 increases upon auxin removal (Figure 7C). Specifically, we observed that TRRAP binding progressively reappears at both the IRF7 and IRF9 promoters, in parallel to TRRAP recovery (Figure 7B and C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by CUT&RUN-qPCR data in Figure 7C.

claim: 6 hr after auxin removal, TRRAP occupancy is similar to that observed in control conditions
source: We found that, 6 hr after auxin removal, TRRAP occupancy is similar to that observed in control conditions, suggesting that TRRAP binding is highly dynamic at these promoters.
evidence: This is stated in the results based on CUT&RUN-qPCR data.

claim: Upon auxin removal, IRF9 mRNA levels rapidly stop increasing and progressively decrease back to basal levels
source: In contrast, upon auxin removal, IRF9 mRNA levels rapidly stop increasing and progressively decrease back to basal levels compared with a continuous auxin treatment (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by RT-qPCR data in Figure 7D.

claim: TRRAP reappearance promptly stabilizes the levels of the OAS1 and IFIT1 mRNAs
source: Similarly, TRRAP reappearance promptly stabilizes the levels of the OAS1 and IFIT1 mRNAs, which are indirectly regulated by TRRAP (Figure 5F), whereas their expression continues to increase when TRRAP depletion is sustained (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by RT-qPCR data in Figure 7D.

claim: Re-expressing TRRAP leads to a rapid reversion of the ISG induction phenotype
source: In summary, re-expressing TRRAP leads to a rapid reversion of the ISG induction phenotype.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a conclusion from the auxin washout experiments.

claim: TRRAP and ISG levels dynamically anticorrelate in HCT116 cells
source: Taken together, our kinetic analyses of TRRAP binding and regulatory roles indicate that TRRAP and ISG levels dynamically anticorrelate in HCT116 cells and provide additional evidence for a direct repressive role for TRRAP in IRF9 expression.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a conclusion from the kinetic analyses.

claim: TELO2 promotes TRRAP assembly into functional complexes, SAGA and TIP60
source: Our work defines the contribution of the HSP90 cochaperone TTT to TRRAP functions in human cells. Using an inducible degron for rapid and robust depletion of endogenous proteins, we demonstrate that the TTT subunit TELO2 promotes TRRAP assembly into functional complexes, SAGA and TIP60, and contributes to TRRAP regulatory roles in gene expression.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: Both TELO2 and TRRAP promote proliferation of CRC cells
source: Functional and transcriptomic analyses indicate that both TELO2 and TRRAP promote proliferation of CRC cells and regulate an overlapping set of genes, including MYC targets.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: TRRAP acts as a transcriptional repressor of IRF9, which encodes a subunit of the ISGF3 regulatory complex
source: We also uncovered an unexpected negative role of TRRAP in the expression of a subset of type I ISGs. Notably, we accumulated evidence that TRRAP acts as a transcriptional repressor of IRF9, which encodes a subunit of the ISGF3 regulatory complex.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: TRRAP and its chaperone TTT might contribute to colorectal tumorigenesis by promoting a specific transcriptional program
source: Our findings suggest that TRRAP and its chaperone TTT might contribute to colorectal tumorigenesis by promoting a specific transcriptional program, both as a coactivator of c-MYC and a repressor of specific ISGF3 targets.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a speculative conclusion.

claim: TTT functional roles are conserved between yeast and mammals
source: Altogether, these studies indicate that TTT functional roles are conserved between yeast and mammals.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a conclusion from the comparative analysis.

claim: Despite its lack of catalytic activity, Tra1/TRRAP shares a dedicated chaperone machinery with active PIKK kinases for assembly and function
source: Therefore, despite its lack of catalytic activity, Tra1/TRRAP shares a dedicated chaperone machinery with active PIKK kinases for assembly and function.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a conclusion from the findings.

claim: The requirement of PIKKs for a dedicated cochaperone explains the selection pressure observed on the sequence and domain organization of the Tra1/TRRAP pseudokinase
source: We thus propose that the requirement of PIKKs for a dedicated cochaperone explains the selection pressure observed on the sequence and domain organization of the Tra1/TRRAP pseudokinase.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a speculative proposal.

claim: Assembly of the NuA4/TIP60 and SAGA complexes requires the HSP90 cochaperone TTT
source: Finally, our work indicates that assembly of the NuA4/TIP60 and SAGA complexes requires the HSP90 cochaperone TTT, contributing to the emerging concept that dedicated mechanisms and chaperones control the de novo assembly of transcription complexes.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a conclusion from the findings.

claim: TRRAP is essential for transcription activation by MYC and E2F
source: In agreement, TRRAP is essential for transcription activation by MYC and E2F and contributes to their oncogenic functions during tumorigenesis (McMahon et al., 1998; Park et al., 2001; Bouchard et al., 2001; Lang et al., 2001; Nikiforov et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with supporting citations.

claim: TRRAP contributes to the oncogenic functions of MYC and E2F during tumorigenesis
source: In agreement, TRRAP is essential for transcription activation by MYC and E2F and contributes to their oncogenic functions during tumorigenesis (McMahon et al., 1998; Park et al., 2001; Bouchard et al., 2001; Lang et al., 2001; Nikiforov et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with supporting citations.

claim: TRRAP depletion relieves IRF9 repression, subsequently inducing the transcription of IRF7 and a subset of other U-ISGs, independently of IFN-I signaling
source: Altogether, the rapid kinetics, efficiency, and reversibility of the AID allowed us to deduce a putative sequence of phenotypic events, by which TRRAP depletion would relieve IRF9 repression, subsequently inducing the transcription of IRF7 and a subset of other U-ISGs, independently of IFN-I signaling.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a proposed model based on the experimental findings.

claim: Seven additional U-ISGs are both repressed and bound by TRRAP and thus putative direct targets
source: Nevertheless, we note that seven additional U-ISGs are both repressed and bound by TRRAP and thus putative direct targets (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on the CUT&RUN-seq and RNA-seq data.

claim: TRRAP might directly contribute to the repression of DDX58 (RIG-I), IFIH1 (MDA5), IFIT3, and STAT1
source: These genes encode key components of the IFN-I signaling pathway and include the viral RNA sensors DDX58 (RIG-I) and IFIH1 (MDA5), the signaling adaptor IFIT3, and the ISGF3 transcription complex subunit STAT1. Although we did not test this possibility, TRRAP might directly contribute to their repression, reinforcing its inhibitory effect on IRF7 and IRF9 expression.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a speculative possibility.

claim: Little is known about the regulation of IRF9 expression, both in immune cells and cancer tissues
source: However, so far, little is known about the regulation of IRF9 expression, both in immune cells and cancer tissues (Suprunenko and Hofer, 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: IRF9 is expressed constitutively
source: Gene expression databases indicate that IRF9 is expressed constitutively.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on gene expression databases.

claim: IRF9 regulation primarily occurs at the level of ISGF3 complex formation and nucleocytoplasmic shuttling
source: Accordingly, previous studies demonstrated that its regulation primarily occurs at the level of ISGF3 complex formation and nucleocytoplasmic shuttling (Wang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: ISGF3 activation does not require de novo gene expression
source: ISGF3 activation does not require de novo gene expression, although IFN-I signaling induces expression of IRF9 and other transcription actors in a positive feedback loop.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as established knowledge.

claim: H2A.Z is removed during ISGF3-dependent transcription activation
source: Furthermore, H2A.Z is removed during ISGF3-dependent transcription activation and, conversely, H2A.Z silencing induces ISGF3 recruitment to ISG promoters, ISG mRNA expression, and IFN-stimulated antiviral immunity (Au-Yeung and Horvath, 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: The Tip60 subunit E(Pc) attenuates expression of components of JAK/STAT signaling in Drosophila
source: In contrast, recent work in Drosophila found that the Tip60 subunit E(Pc) attenuates expression of components of JAK/STAT signaling (Bailetti et al., 2019), which is reminiscent of our findings and suggests that this function of TRRAP might be conserved in other eukaryotic species.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: The SAGA subunit GCN5/PCAF represses IFN-I signaling by inhibiting the TBK1 kinase
source: Finally, genetic and biochemical evidence indicates that the SAGA subunit GCN5/PCAF represses IFN-I signaling by inhibiting the TBK1 kinase, which targets IRF3 (Jin et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: TRRAP functions by a distinct mechanism from GCN5/PCAF in the context of CRC HCT116 cells
source: In contrast, we observed that TRRAP depletion induces ISG expression without IRF3 phosphorylation and activation of IFN signaling, demonstrating that TRRAP functions by a distinct mechanism in the context of CRC HCT116 cells.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a conclusion from the experimental findings.

claim: TRRAP is recurrently overexpressed in CRC patient samples
source: Supporting this conclusion, TRRAP is recurrently overexpressed in CRC patient samples (our analysis of the COADREAD cohort, http://xena.ucsc.edu/), and we show here that TRRAP depletion primarily affects a MYC target signature in HCT116 cells.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on analysis of patient data.

claim: TRRAP might contribute to colorectal tumorigenesis by restricting ISG expression levels
source: In addition, our work suggests that TRRAP might also contribute to colorectal tumorigenesis by restricting ISG expression levels.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a speculative suggestion.

claim: ISGs are normally repressed in CRC cells, but upregulated upon acquisition of radio- and chemoresistance
source: Indeed, several studies reported that ISGs are normally repressed in CRC cells, but upregulated upon acquisition of radio- and chemoresistance (Cheon et al., 2013; Gongora et al., 2008; Khodarev et al., 2004; Weichselbaum et al., 2008; Khodarev et al., 2007; Fryknäs et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with multiple supporting citations.

claim: The interferon-related DNA damage signature (IRDS) is virtually identical to the subset of ISGs induced by unphosphorylated U-ISGF3 and those repressed by TRRAP in HCT116 CRC cells
source: Remarkably, the IRDS is virtually identical to the subset of ISGs induced by unphosphorylated U-ISGF3 and those repressed by TRRAP in HCT116 CRC cells.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an observation from comparing gene sets.

claim: TRRAP might play a new role in colorectal tumorigenesis by repressing a subset of ISGs
source: Therefore, TRRAP might play a new role in colorectal tumorigenesis by repressing a subset of ISGs.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a speculative conclusion.

claim: CUT&RUN avoids formaldehyde crosslinking and generates very little noise
source: Overall, CUT&RUN avoids formaldehyde crosslinking, which can yield misleading results and mask epitopes, and generates very little noise because undigested chromatin and genomic DNA are not extracted.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a description of the CUT&RUN method.

claim: MYC binds to a large region of the MIR17-HG promoter in human K562 chronic myeloid leukemia cells
source: Analysis of published MYC CUT&RUN-seq data confirmed that it binds to a large region of the MIR17-HG promoter in human K562 chronic myeloid leukemia cells (Skene and Henikoff, 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the results with a supporting citation.

claim: MYC binds to the promoter of MIR17-HG in HCT116 cells
source: In agreement, using conventional quantitative PCR of DNA fragments released after an anti-MYC CUT&RUN analysis, we found that MYC binds to the promoter of MIR17-HG in HCT116 cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A), validating our protocol.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by CUT&RUN-qPCR data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: TRRAP binding at MIR17HG is about 60-fold above that observed using control rabbit IgGs
source: Indeed, we observed a strong footprint signal of TRRAP at the promoter region of MIR17-HG. Comparison with several negative controls confirmed the robustness and specificity of this observation. First, TRRAP binding at MIR17HG is about 60-fold above that observed using control rabbit IgGs.
evidence: This is stated in the results based on CUT&RUN-qPCR data.

claim: TRRAP depletion reduces the binding of MYC to MIR17-HG
source: Interestingly, TRRAP depletion also reduces the binding of MYC to MIR17-HG, suggesting that TRRAP contributes to MYC recruitment to promoters (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by CUT&RUN-qPCR data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Statistical analysis of enriched genomic regions identified 22,219 peaks of TRRAP binding
source: Statistical analysis of enriched genomic regions using the MACS2 algorithm (Zhang et al., 2008) identified 22,219 peaks of TRRAP binding, which decreased down to 849 peaks upon auxin-mediated TRRAP depletion (Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is stated in the results based on CUT&RUN-seq data analysis.

claim: TRRAP binds mostly within about 300 base pairs (bp) of the TSS
source: Plotting the distribution of the position of each peak relative to the position of the nearest TSS revealed that TRRAP binds mostly within about 300 base pairs (bp) of the TSS (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by the histogram in Figure 5A.

claim: TRRAP predominantly binds promoter-proximal regions
source: This range corresponds to the median size of nucleosome-depleted regions (NDRs) measured by NOMe-seq in HCT116 cells (Lay et al., 2015), indicating that TRRAP predominantly binds promoter-proximal regions.
evidence: This is stated in the results based on comparison with published data.

claim: CUT&RUN is an efficient and robust method to profile the genome-wide occupancy of endogenous TRRAP in human cells
source: We conclude that CUT&RUN is an efficient and robust method to profile the genome-wide occupancy of endogenous TRRAP, a component of large chromatin-modifying and -remodeling complexes, in human cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a conclusion from the CUT&RUN-seq experiments.

claim: TRRAP binds to most genes that are detectably expressed in proliferating HCT116 cells
source: Visualization on a heatmap ranked by basal transcript levels demonstrated that TRRAP binds to most genes that are detectably expressed in proliferating HCT116 cells (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by the heatmap in Figure 5B.

claim: TRRAP enrichment appears to correlate positively with transcript level
source: TRRAP enrichment appears to correlate positively with transcript level, suggesting a global role in RNA polymerase II transcription, as shown for yeast SAGA and NuA4 (Baptista et al., 2017; Bruzzone et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the results as an observation from the heatmap and supported by citations.

claim: About three-quarter of TRRAP-regulated genes are bound by TRRAP (1690/2227)
source: We found that about three-quarter of TRRAP-regulated genes are bound by TRRAP (1690/2227) and therefore candidates for being direct targets.
evidence: This is stated in the results based on overlap analysis of CUT&RUN-seq and RNA-seq data.

claim: A majority of activated genes are bound by TRRAP (83%, 1066/1277)
source: Venn diagram and heatmap visualizations showed that a majority of activated genes are bound by TRRAP (83%, 1066/1277) as expected for a transcriptional coactivator.
evidence: This is stated in the results based on overlap analysis of CUT&RUN-seq and RNA-seq data.

claim: A smaller fraction of repressed genes has a TRRAP peak within or near their promoter (66%, 624/950)
source: In contrast, a smaller fraction of repressed genes has a TRRAP peak within or near their promoter (66%, 624/950).
evidence: This is stated in the results based on overlap analysis of CUT&RUN-seq and RNA-seq data.

claim: Only 16% of genes (211/1277) are presumably indirectly activated by TRRAP
source: Conversely, only 16% of genes (211/1277) are presumably indirectly activated by TRRAP, whereas a higher fraction of genes, about one-third (326/950), are indirectly repressed.
evidence: This is stated in the results based on overlap analysis of CUT&RUN-seq and RNA-seq data.

claim: About one-third of genes (326/950) are indirectly repressed by TRRAP
source: Conversely, only 16% of genes (211/1277) are presumably indirectly activated by TRRAP, whereas a higher fraction of genes, about one-third (326/950), are indirectly repressed.
evidence: This is stated in the results based on overlap analysis of CUT&RUN-seq and RNA-seq data.

claim: Combining RNA-seq and CUT&RUN-seq analyses with a conditional depletion allele identified about 1690 genes that are candidate targets of TRRAP in proliferating HCT116 cells
source: To summarize, combining RNA-seq and CUT&RUN-seq analyses with a conditional depletion allele allowed us to identify a total of about 1690 genes that are candidate targets of TRRAP in proliferating HCT116 cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a summary of the findings.
